course.title: Bead Making and Jewellery
course.tagline: Make beaded necklaces, bracelets and waist beads people love to wear.

days.title: Jewellery Making Basics
days.goal: Know the tools and materials of bead jewellery.

video.title: 5 Essential Jewelry Making Techniques

steps: Learn the tools: pliers, cutters, beading needle and thread.
Learn the materials: beads, cord, clasps and findings (the small metal parts).
Learn bead sizes: small beads are 4mm, big beads are 10mm.
Set up a bead mat so beads do not roll away.
days.task: Label your tools and materials.
days.challenge: Name three tools and what each does.

quiz.q: What are findings in jewellery making?
options: The small metal parts like clasps and rings
quiz.explain: Findings are the small metal parts: clasps, jump rings and hooks.

quiz.q: Why use a bead mat?
options: So beads do not roll away
quiz.explain: A bead mat has a soft surface that stops beads rolling off the table.

quiz.q: What size is a small bead?
quiz.explain: Small beads are about 4mm across; big beads are about 10mm.

days.title: Bead Types: Glass, Wood, Stone and Plastic
days.goal: Tell bead types apart and know what each suits.

video.title: 5 Essential Jewelry Making Techniques

steps: Hold glass, wood, stone and plastic beads.
Learn that glass beads shine and suit necklaces.
Learn that wood beads are light and suit casual bracelets.
Learn that stone beads are heavy and suit statement pieces.
days.task: Sort beads into glass, wood, stone and plastic.
days.challenge: Pick the best bead type for a bracelet and explain why.

quiz.q: Which beads suit a casual bracelet?
quiz.explain: Wood beads are light and suit casual everyday bracelets.

quiz.q: Why are stone beads heavy?
quiz.explain: Stone is dense, so stone beads feel heavy compared with wood or plastic.

quiz.q: Which beads shine the most?
quiz.explain: Glass beads catch light and shine, so they suit necklaces.

days.title: Stringing Beads
days.goal: String beads on cord in a neat pattern.

video.title: 5 Essential Jewelry Making Techniques

steps: Cut cord a little longer than you need.
Thread beads in your pattern, checking the colours.
Keep the beads snug with no gaps.
Tie a strong knot and hide it inside a bead.
days.task: String a bracelet with a neat pattern.
days.challenge: String beads with no gaps and no loose cord.

quiz.q: How long should you cut the cord when stringing beads?
options: A little longer than you need
quiz.explain: Cut cord a little longer than you need so you have room to tie the knot.

quiz.q: How should the beads sit on the cord?
quiz.explain: Keep the beads snug with no gaps so the pattern looks neat.

quiz.q: What should you do with the knot after tying it?
quiz.explain: Tie a strong knot and hide it inside a bead so it is safe and does not show.

days.title: Bracelet Sizes and Fit
days.goal: Measure wrists and make bracelets that fit.

video.title: How to measure wrist & bracelet sizes! Perfect bracelets every time + tips for a secure knot

steps: Measure a wrist with a tape around the bone.
Add about 1cm for comfort.
Learn that a tight bracelet is uncomfortable and breaks easily.
Test the fit on a real wrist before you finish.
days.task: Measure three wrists and record the sizes.
days.challenge: Make a bracelet that fits a wrist well.

quiz.q: Where do you measure a wrist for a bracelet?
quiz.explain: Measure a wrist with a tape around the bone.

quiz.q: How much extra should you add for comfort?
quiz.explain: Add about 1cm for comfort.

quiz.q: Why should a bracelet not be too tight?
options: It is uncomfortable and breaks easily
quiz.explain: A tight bracelet is uncomfortable and breaks easily. Test the fit on a real wrist before you finish.

days.title: Pearl Necklaces
days.goal: String a pearl necklace that sits well.

video.title: Pearl Knotting Using Tweezers
video.channel: Beadaholique - Your Home for Beading Inspiration

steps: Learn that pearls need a knot between each one so they do not rub.
String pearls with knots using a beading needle.
Add a clasp that is easy to open.
Check the necklace hangs evenly.
days.task: String a short pearl necklace with knots.
days.challenge: Knot between pearls so they do not rub.

quiz.q: Why put a knot between each pearl?
options: So the pearls do not rub each other
quiz.explain: Pearls need a knot between each one so they do not rub.

quiz.q: What tool do you use to string pearls with knots?
quiz.explain: String pearls with knots using a beading needle.

quiz.q: How should you check a finished pearl necklace?
quiz.explain: Check the necklace hangs evenly before you finish.

days.title: Clasps and Findings
days.goal: Fit clasps and findings so jewellery opens and closes well.

video.title: How to Attach a Clasp - Make a Beaded Bracelet - Jewellery Making Tutorial

steps: Learn the clasp types: lobster, toggle and magnetic.
Learn that a jump ring is a small metal ring that joins parts.
Open a jump ring sideways, never pull it apart.
Test the clasp three times before you finish.
days.task: Fit a lobster clasp to a bracelet.
days.challenge: Open and close a jump ring the right way.

quiz.q: What are the three clasp types you learned?
quiz.explain: Learn the clasp types: lobster, toggle and magnetic.

quiz.q: What is a jump ring?
options: A small metal ring that joins parts
quiz.explain: A jump ring is a small metal ring that joins parts.

quiz.q: How should you open a jump ring?
options: Twist it sideways, never pull it apart
quiz.explain: Open a jump ring sideways, never pull it apart. Test the clasp three times before you finish.

days.title: Project: Make a Beaded Bracelet Set
days.goal: Make a set of three beaded bracelets that match.

video.title: DIY Beaded Bracelet

steps: Pick beads in colours that go together.
Make three bracelets in different patterns.
Fit clasps and check the sizes.
Present the set neatly on a card or cloth.
days.task: Finish a set of three matching bracelets.
days.challenge: Make three bracelets with three patterns that still match.

quiz.q: How many bracelets are in the bracelet set?
quiz.explain: Make a set of three beaded bracelets that match.

quiz.q: How should the three bracelets be different?
options: Different patterns, but colours that go together
They should all be the same
quiz.explain: Pick beads in colours that go together and make three bracelets in different patterns.

quiz.q: What should you check before you present the set?
options: The clasps work and the sizes fit
The beads are all the same colour
The bracelets are all the same pattern
The card is the biggest one
quiz.explain: Fit clasps and check the sizes, then present the set neatly on a card or cloth.

project.title: Make a Beaded Bracelet Set
project.brief: Make a set of three beaded bracelets that match.

days.title: Florere Bracelet
days.goal: Make a Florere bracelet with a flower pattern.

video.title: DIY Beaded Bracelet

steps: Learn the Florere pattern: beads in a flower shape.
Follow the pattern step by step, one petal at a time.
Keep the thread tension even so the flower sits flat.
Finish with a clasp and check the shape.
days.task: Make a Florere bracelet with a clear flower pattern.
days.challenge: Make a flower pattern that sits flat.

quiz.q: What is the Florere pattern?
quiz.explain: Learn the Florere pattern: beads in a flower shape.

quiz.q: How should you follow the pattern?
options: Step by step, one petal at a time
quiz.explain: Follow the pattern step by step, one petal at a time.

quiz.q: Why keep the thread tension even?
quiz.explain: Keep the thread tension even so the flower sits flat.

days.title: Bead Patterns and Colour
days.goal: Design bead patterns with colour that works.

video.title: DIY Beaded Bracelet

steps: Learn that warm colours (red, orange) feel bold.
Learn that cool colours (blue, green) feel calm.
Use one main colour, one second colour and a small accent.
Draw your pattern on paper before you bead.
days.task: Draw a bead pattern with three colours.
days.challenge: Design a pattern with colours that work together.

quiz.q: How do warm colours like red and orange feel?
quiz.explain: Warm colours (red, orange) feel bold.

quiz.q: How do cool colours like blue and green feel?
quiz.explain: Cool colours (blue, green) feel calm.

quiz.q: What should you do before you start beading a pattern?
options: Draw your pattern on paper first
quiz.explain: Draw your pattern on paper before you bead. Use one main colour, one second colour and a small accent.

days.title: Woven Cuff Bracelets
days.goal: Weave beads into a wide cuff bracelet.

video.title: How to Make a Florere Bracelet

steps: Weaving means passing thread through beads in rows.
Set up a bead loom (a frame that holds threads) or weave by hand.
Weave row by row, keeping the rows straight.
Finish the edges neatly and add a clasp.
days.task: Weave a small cuff bracelet.
days.challenge: Weave rows that stay straight and even.

quiz.q: What does weaving beads mean?
options: Passing thread through beads in rows
quiz.explain: Weaving means passing thread through beads in rows.

quiz.q: What is a bead loom?
options: A frame that holds threads for weaving beads
quiz.explain: A bead loom is a frame that holds threads. You can also weave by hand.

quiz.q: How should you weave the rows?
options: Row by row, keeping the rows straight
quiz.explain: Weave row by row, keeping the rows straight, then finish the edges neatly and add a clasp.

days.title: Wire Wrapping Basics
days.goal: Wrap wire around beads to hold them.

video.title: How to Make a Florere Bracelet

steps: Wire wrapping means bending wire to hold a bead.
Use round-nose pliers to make loops.
Make a loop, thread a bead, then close the loop.
Keep loops the same size for a neat look.
days.task: Wrap wire around three beads with neat loops.
days.challenge: Make loops that are all the same size.

quiz.q: What is wire wrapping?
options: Bending wire to hold a bead
quiz.explain: Wire wrapping bends wire around a bead to hold it in place.

quiz.q: Why make loops the same size?
quiz.explain: Matching loops make the jewellery look professional.

quiz.q: What tool makes wire loops?
quiz.explain: Round-nose pliers bend wire into smooth round loops.

days.title: Beaded Earrings
days.goal: Make a pair of beaded earrings.

video.title: How to Make a Florere Bracelet

steps: Pick beads light enough for ears.
Make two earrings the same: same beads, same order.
Fit ear hooks and check they hang evenly.
Test the pair: they should match and feel light.
days.task: Make a pair of matching beaded earrings.
days.challenge: Make two earrings that are exactly the same.

quiz.q: What kind of beads should you pick for earrings?
quiz.explain: Pick beads light enough for ears.

quiz.q: How should the two earrings compare?
options: The same: same beads, same order
quiz.explain: Make two earrings the same: same beads, same order.

quiz.q: What should you check after fitting the ear hooks?
options: That they hang evenly and feel light
quiz.explain: Fit ear hooks and check they hang evenly. The pair should match and feel light.

days.title: Gemstone Cluster Bracelet
days.goal: Make a bracelet with clusters of small gemstones.

video.title: How to Make Woven Cuff Bracelets

steps: A cluster is a group of small beads bunched together.
Wire small gemstones into clusters.
Join clusters along the bracelet.
Check the bracelet is not too heavy to wear.
days.task: Make a bracelet with gemstone clusters.
days.challenge: Make clusters that are even and secure.

quiz.q: What is a cluster in jewellery making?
options: A group of small beads bunched together
quiz.explain: A cluster is a group of small beads bunched together.

quiz.q: How do you make a gemstone cluster?
options: Wire small gemstones together into a bunch
quiz.explain: Wire small gemstones into clusters, then join the clusters along the bracelet.

quiz.q: What should you check on a finished cluster bracelet?
options: That it is not too heavy to wear
That all clusters are the same colour
quiz.explain: Check the bracelet is not too heavy to wear.

days.title: Project: Make a Woven Cuff Bracelet
days.goal: Weave a wide cuff bracelet and finish it neatly.

video.title: How to Make Woven Cuff Bracelets

steps: Pick a pattern and colours for the cuff.
Weave row by row until the cuff is wide enough.
Finish the edges and add a clasp.
Check the cuff fits and sits flat on the wrist.
days.task: Finish a woven cuff bracelet that fits well.
days.challenge: Weave a cuff with a clear pattern.

quiz.q: What should you pick first for a woven cuff?
quiz.explain: Pick a pattern and colours for the cuff before you start weaving.

quiz.q: When do you stop weaving the cuff?
options: When it is as wide as your arm
quiz.explain: Weave row by row until the cuff is wide enough.

quiz.q: What should you check on the finished cuff?
options: That it fits and sits flat on the wrist
quiz.explain: Check the cuff fits and sits flat on the wrist.

project.title: Make a Woven Cuff Bracelet
project.brief: Weave a wide cuff bracelet and finish it neatly.

days.title: Necklace Lengths

video.title: How to Make Woven Cuff Bracelets

steps: A choker sits high on the neck, about 35cm.
A princess length sits on the collarbone, about 45cm.
A matinee length sits on the chest, about 55cm.
Measure the length before you cut the cord.
days.task: Make necklaces in two different lengths.
days.challenge: Pick the right length for a necklace and explain why.

quiz.q: How long is a choker necklace?
quiz.explain: A choker sits high on the neck at about 35cm.

quiz.q: How long is a princess necklace?
quiz.explain: Princess length sits on the collarbone at about 45cm.

quiz.q: Why measure necklace length before cutting cord?
options: So the necklace sits where you want it
quiz.explain: Measuring first means the necklace ends at the right place on the body.

days.title: Wire Earrings
days.goal: Make wire-wrapped earrings with beads.

video.title: How to Make Wire Wrapped and Beaded Earrings

steps: Wrap wire around a bead to make a drop.
Make two drops the same size.
Fit ear hooks and check they match.
Polish the wire so it shines.
days.task: Make a pair of wire-wrapped earrings.
days.challenge: Make two drops that match exactly.

quiz.q: How do you make a wire earring drop?
options: Glue the bead to a hook
quiz.explain: Wrap wire around a bead to make a drop.

quiz.q: How should the two drops compare?

quiz.q: What should you do to the wire at the end?

days.title: Waist Beads: The Tradition

video.title: How to Make Wire Wrapped and Beaded Earrings

steps: Waist beads are strands worn around the waist, common in African culture.
They can be worn for beauty, confidence or tradition.
They are made on strong cord, not elastic, for a lasting fit.
Measure the waist at the navel for the right size.
days.task: Explain waist beads to a customer in plain words.
days.challenge: Measure a waist for waist beads.

quiz.q: What are waist beads?
quiz.explain: Waist beads are strands worn around the waist, common in African culture.

quiz.q: What are waist beads worn for?
quiz.explain: They can be worn for beauty, confidence or tradition.

quiz.q: Where do you measure for waist beads?
options: At the waist at the navel
quiz.explain: Measure the waist at the navel for the right size.

steps: Cut elastic cord longer than the waist size.
Thread beads in your pattern.

days.challenge: Make a strand that fits and sits flat.

quiz.q: How long should you cut the elastic cord for waist beads?

quiz.explain: Tie a strong knot and hide it inside a bead.

quiz.q: What should you check on the finished waist beads?

quiz.q: What cord do you use for waist beads without elastic?

quiz.q: Why are non-elastic waist beads tied on?
